A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 15 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v3, including supplementary materials, were readable, and their text, figures, tables and equations support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original five-task coding benchmarks, feature statistics, truncation ablations and cross-task generalization experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original coding benchmarks, ablations, feature analyses, cross-task transfer results and encoding/decoding measurements.

M1.justification: The codecs, split points, packing and rate-distortion loss are retained. However, v1 Figure 4 explicitly restricts preprocessing quantization/dequantization to VTM, whereas v3 removes that restriction and Section 8.2.1 describes quantizing training features. The PDFs do not clearly resolve whether Hyperprior preprocessing actually changed or its documentation became inconsistent.

E1.justification: The five primary tasks and source datasets remain, including OpenBookQA in training. ImageNet coverage nevertheless expands from 100 to 500 distinct represented classes in Section 4.1.3. Other increases in sample counts within retained task coverage primarily concern E3.

E2.justification: VTM and Hyperprior remain the principal codecs. However, the generalizability comparison includes VTM in v1 Table 10 but only Hyperprior variants in v3 Table 6. Table 3 also replaces the 10-bit Quantization reference with a 32-bit Original reference.

E3.justification: Test counts increase from 100/20/16/100/100 to 500/100/80/500/500 across the five tasks. FID replaces CLIP Score, and TTI is excluded from accuracy-drop evaluation. Transfer and timing protocols also change. The training table revises one CSR lambda from 0.045 to 0.15, although v3's timing table inconsistently lists 0.07.

E4.justification: v3 adds encoding/decoding complexity analysis and replaces Cls–Seg generalization testing with a Seg/CSR/TTI transfer matrix spanning heterogeneous features. The truncation ablations remain unchanged as Tables 10–11 rather than disappearing. Conversely, v1's reported training instability when cropping CSR features to 64 × 512 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point results and descriptive feature statistics without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new timing results likewise provide no uncertainty estimates; the ten-example sampling practice for feature statistics remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 extensively replaces numerical results: its highest-rate VTM classification row changes from 1.90 BPFP/100% accuracy to 1.94 BPFP/99.80%. Table 5's VTM depth correlation changes from 0.9904 to 0.8549. New FID, timing and transfer results are reported. Revised test subsets and metrics prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The BPFP and accuracy-drop definitions remain unchanged. The identical rate-distortion loss moves from v1 Section 9.2.2 to v3 Section 6.1.2. Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same central contributions: a large-model feature dataset covering three models and five tasks, unified test conditions, and two adapted coding baselines with benchmarks. v3's emphasis on establishing a research area and assessing baseline applicability retains the existing scientific scope.

C2.justification: The distortion–accuracy explanation shifts from depth/RMSE correlation to TTI/image-codec compatibility. New discussion develops the tradeoffs between VTM runtime, Hyperprior GPU efficiency and cross-task generalizability, including hardware and implementation qualifications. The earlier explanation of CSR cropping failure is removed.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future-release promise with a concrete code/data repository pointer and availability statement, whose external availability was not checked. v3 newly specifies timing hardware and Hyperprior's single input/output channel, while retaining most packing and training details. It removes the explicit statement that task-head weights come from pretrained models.

R1.justification: v3 adds three cited works: Rethinking the Joint Optimization in Video Coding for Machines, Feature Compression with 3D Sparse Convolution, and Perceptual Image Compression with Conditional Diffusion Transformers. These modestly extend the background citations without materially changing the research positioning or adding evaluated codec families.

P1.justification: Prose is extensively edited across the introduction, background, deployment discussion, dataset rationale and conclusion. Section 6 is reorganized around baseline applicability, complexity and generalizability; packing merges with preprocessing, the loss moves into the main text, and appendix sections are reordered and subdivided.

P2.justification: The evidence displays are substantially reorganized: v3 adds a runtime table and restructures transfer tables and plots, removes v1's linear-fit panels and most standalone rate–accuracy panels, redraws Figure 5 without TTI, and relocates ablation and dataset-analysis displays. Several feature heatmaps and plot scales also change.

improvement.justification: Expanded sampling, broader transfer tests and new timing measurements make the benchmark more useful and better support its deployment tradeoffs (v3 Tables 1, 6 and 8). The repository pointer improves access information. These gains are tempered by ambiguous Hyperprior quantization documentation and inconsistent CSR lambdas in Tables 7 and 8. Replacing CLIP Score with FID does not itself establish improved performance.
